# AWS DataSync

Store S3 and EFS locations and Basic tasks; execute persistent, queued local S3-to-S3 copies with filtering, deletion and verification.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `datasync` |
| Signing name | `datasync` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2018-11-09` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Background local S3-to-S3 copies; EFS locations and schedules are records only |
| Selected operations | 20 of 53 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-datasync) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Agents require real appliance activation; agents, NFS and SMB locations (required agent references), HDFS, FSx, object storage and Azure Blob locations are unsupported.
- Storage system discovery, Enhanced mode, manifests, task reports and UpdateTaskExecution are unsupported.
- EFS locations are records only; StartTaskExecution explicitly rejects any non-S3 location.
- Schedules, LogLevel and filesystem metadata options are stored only: no scheduled execution, CloudWatch log delivery or filesystem metadata application; bandwidth throttling is rejected except the unlimited -1 default.
- No distributed S3 snapshot: concurrent source changes can fail verification; cancellation or a process interruption may leave copies from the current batch of up to 100 objects applied before progress commits, and restart repeats that batch.
- No S3 access-point or Outposts locations, multipart copy, remote AWS access or IAM role assumption; S3 service local object size and storage behavior apply.
- Queue processing is FIFO per task using persisted sequence keys; progress counters model selected objects and bytes, with no network compression or measured phase durations.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
